english: Let $f:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ be a function such that $f(xy)=f(x)+f(y)$ for all $x,y\in(0,\infty)$ and $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to1}\dfrac{f(x)}{x-1}=3$. Then the value of $\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\sum_{r=1}^{n}\dfrac{r}{n^{2}}\,f\left(\dfrac{r}{n}\right)$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $f:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ एक फलन है, जिसके लिए सभी $x,y\in(0,\infty)$ के लिए $f(xy)=f(x)+f(y)$ है तथा $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to1}\dfrac{f(x)}{x-1}=3$ है। तब $\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\sum_{r=1}^{n}\dfrac{r}{n^{2}}\,f\left(\dfrac{r}{n}\right)$ का मान ______ है।
solution_full: Putting $x=y=1$ gives $f(1)=2f(1)$, so $f(1)=0$. The given limit is then $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to1}\dfrac{f(x)-f(1)}{x-1}=3$, i.e. $f'(1)=3$.
For $x>0$: $f(x+t)=f\left(x\left(1+\dfrac tx\right)\right)=f(x)+f\left(1+\dfrac tx\right)$, so $\dfrac{f(x+t)-f(x)}{t}=\dfrac1x\cdot\dfrac{f\left(1+\frac tx\right)}{t/x}\to\dfrac{3}{x}$ as $t\to0$.

The sum is $\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{n}\dfrac1n\cdot\dfrac rn\cdot3\log_e\dfrac rn$, a Riemann sum of $F(x)=3x\log_e x$ on $[0,1]$ with right end points. $F$ extends continuously to $[0,1]$ with $F(0)=0$, since $x\log_e x\to0$ as $x\to0^{+}$; so the limit equals $\displaystyle\int_0^1 3x\log_e x\,dx$.

By parts, $\displaystyle\int_0^1 x\log_e x\,dx=\left[\dfrac{x^{2}}{2}\log_e x\right]_0^1-\int_0^1\dfrac{x^{2}}{2}\cdot\dfrac1x\,dx=0-\dfrac14=-\dfrac14$, the boundary term at $0$ vanishing because $x^{2}\log_e x\to0$.
Hence the limit is $3\cdot\left(-\dfrac14\right)=-\dfrac34=-0.75$ (a direct computation with $n=200000$ gives $-0.7499999$).
originality_note: New: the logarithmic Cauchy equation fixed only by a limit at 1, fed into a weighted Riemann sum whose integrand has a removable end-point behaviour at 0 (way 5). Closest known: f(xy)=f(x)+f(y) with f'(1) given, asking f(e) or f'(x). Different because: the recovered function is never asked directly; it must be turned into a limit of a sum and an integral with a log singularity.

concept_use.Cauchy’s Functional Equations: Standard: f(xy)=f(x)+f(y) gives f(1)=0 and f'(x)=f'(1)/x, so f(x)=3 ln x.
concept_use.Definite integrals combined with limits: The limit of the sum is converted into the definite integral of 3x ln x over [0,1], evaluated by parts as -3/4.

stem_review: Read as a student: domain stated; the limit condition defines f'(1) because f(1)=0 follows from the equation. Answer -0.75 checked symbolically and by a direct sum with n=200000. Negative decimal as planned, exact to two places. Changed: No change.
key_step: Recovering f=3 ln x from the limit condition, then reading the sum as the integral of 3x ln x on [0,1].
justification: Two linked standard ideas (Cauchy equation via derivative at 1, limit of a sum as an integral) plus by-parts with an end-point limit, no options. Comparable to 2023-P2-Q1 (L2) for the integral-equation chain, raised by the numerical format and the sum-to-integral step; near 2025-P2-Q14 (L3).
blueprint_concepts: Cauchy’s Functional Equations: Standard forms like f(x+y)=f(x)f(y), f(xy)=f(x)+f(y)
